newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch up, seen in sideways trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch up, seen in sideways trend.

text.p: Polish shares on Tuesday inched up after Monday's slight fall and analysts said the market could gain again on Wednesday and stay in its six-week-long flat trend.

They said the central bank head's statement in the Nowa Europa daily on Tuesday that interest rates might rise if fast credit growth continues might not have had a significant effect on shares as the bank had long wanted real rates to rise.

"It seems no falls threaten because at today's session -- despite the information in the newspaper that rates could rise -- the market reacted calmly," said Ryszard Sikora, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.4 percent to 13,717.8 points and turnover rose 18.1 percent to 88.8 million zlotys ($31.1 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 45 to 28 with 10 stocks stable.
Analysts said Tuesday's news that last month's industrial output fell 7.3 percent after rising seven percent in October was not a bad sign considering there were three fewer workdays in November.

Analysts said biggest loser insurer Polisa, down 9.6 percent in light trade, may be subject to significant price swings because of the listing of some of its shares on Poland's nascent regulated over-the-counter market.
They said food producer Sokolow, up seven percent in active trade, was fundamentally solid and enjoying seasonal gains.
Continuous trade turnover was at 5.7 million zlotys ($2 million) with five stocks up and three flat.

Mass privatisation NFI units were flat at 138.5 zlotys ($48.5) in both regular and continuous trade in turnovers of 17.5 million zlotys ($6.1 million) and 16.3 million zlotys ($5.7 million) respectively.
